papers.title: 3D bioprinting of triphasic nanocomposite hydrogels and scaffolds for cell adhesion and migration.
papers.abstract: In this study we describe the first example of 3D bioprinted triphasic chiral nanocomposite (NC) hydrogels/scaffolds to simulate the complex 3D architecture, nano/micro scale topography, and chiral nature of extracellular matrix. These multifunctional constructs are prepared using a 3D bioprinting technique and are composed of three connected hydrogels/scaffolds, two of which are loaded with nanomaterials functionalized with opposite enantiomers of a biomolecule. With these constructs, we direct the migration of cells toward the part of the triphasic chiral NC hydrogels/scaffolds containing the cells' preferred biomolecule enantiomer.

summary_en.motivation: To mimic the complex 3D architecture and chiral nature of the extracellular matrix for guiding cell behavior.
summary_en.method: Triphasic chiral nanocomposite hydrogels/scaffolds were fabricated via 3D bioprinting with enantiomer-functionalized nanomaterials.
summary_en.result: The constructs successfully directed cell migration toward regions containing the cells' preferred biomolecule enantiomer.
summary_en.validation: Cell migration assays demonstrated the selective guidance capability of the printed scaffolds.

papers.title: Cryogenic free-form extrusion bioprinting of decellularized small intestinal submucosa for potential applications in skin tissue engineering.
papers.abstract: A novel strategy of cryogenic 3D bioprinting assisted by free-from extrusion printing has been developed and applied to printing of a decellularized small intestinal submucosa (dSIS) slurry. The rheological properties, including kinetic viscosity, storage modulus (G'), and loss modulus (G″), were appropriate for free-from extrusion printing of dSIS slurry. Three different groups of scaffolds, including P500, P600, and P700, with filament distances of 500, 600, and 700 μm, respectively were fabricated at a 5 mm s-1 working velocity of the platform (V xy) and 25 kPa air pressure of the dispensing system (P) at -20 °C. The fabricated scaffolds were crosslinked via 1-ethyl-3-(3-dimethylaminopropyl) carbodiimide (EDC) which resulted in a polyporous microstructure. The variations in the filament diameter and pore size were evaluated in the initial frozen state after printing, the lyophilized state, and after immersion in a PBS solution. The Young's modulus of the P500, P600, and P700 scaffolds was measured in wet and dry states for EDC-crosslinked scaffolds. The cell experiment results showed improved cell adhesion, viability, and proliferation both on the surface and within the scaffold, indicating the biocompatibility and suitability of the scaffold for 3D cell models. Further, gene and protein expression of normal skin fibroblasts on dSIS scaffolds demonstrated their ability to promote the production of some extracellular matrix proteins (i.e. collagen I, collagen III, and fibronectin) in vitro. Overall, this study presents a new potential strategy, by combining cryogenic 3D bioprinting with decellularized extracellular matrix materials, to manufacture ideal scaffolds for skin tissue engineering applications.

summary_zh.method: 利用自由挤出打印在-20°C下制造不同丝间距的dSIS支架，并用EDC交联。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a cryogenic free-form extrusion bioprinting method for decellularized small intestinal submucosa (dSIS) for skin tissue engineering applications.
summary_en.method: dSIS slurry was printed at -20°C with varying filament distances (500, 600, 700 μm) and crosslinked with EDC to form porous scaffolds.
summary_en.result: The fabricated scaffolds exhibited suitable rheological properties, porous microstructure, and supported fibroblast adhesion, viability, proliferation, and extracellular matrix production.
summary_en.validation: In vitro cell experiments and mechanical testing in wet and dry states confirmed biocompatibility and adequate Young's modulus.

papers.title: Impact of Different Titanium Implant Thread Designs on Bone Healing: A Biomechanical and Histometric Study with an Animal Model.
papers.abstract: Threads of dental implants with healing chamber configurations have become a target to improve osseointegration. This biomechanical and histometric study aimed to evaluate the influence of implant healing chamber configurations on the torque removal value (RTv), percentage of bone-to-implant contact (BIC%), bone fraction occupancy inside the thread area (BAFO%), and bone and osteocyte density (Ost) in the rabbit tibia after two months of healing. Titanium implants with three different thread configurations were evaluated: Group 1 (G1), with a conventional "v" thread-shaped implant design; Group 2 (G2), with square threads; and Group 3 (G3), the experimental group with longer threads (healing chamber). Ten rabbits (4.5 ± 0.5 kg) received three implants in each tibia (one per group), distributed in a randomized manner. After a period of two months, the tibia blocks (implants and the surrounding tissue) were removed and processed for ground sectioning to evaluate BIC%, BAFO%, and osteocyte density. The ANOVA one-way statistical test was used followed by the Bonferoni's multiple comparison test to determine individual difference among groups, considering a statistical difference when p < 0.05. Histometric evaluation showed a higher BAFO% values and Ost density for G3 in comparison with the other two groups (G1 and G2), with p < 0.05. However, the RTv and BIC% parameters were not significantly different between groups (p > 0.05). The histological data suggest that the healing chambers in the implant macrogeometry can improve the bone reaction in comparison with the conventional thread design.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及钛植入体螺纹设计对骨愈合的影响，但未涉及增材制造（AM）或多孔结构，与AM生物医学材料方向不相关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not involve additive manufacturing (LPBF), porous structures, stress shielding, fatigue testing, or surface roughness characterization; it uses machined implants and focuses on thread design in a dental context.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究不同螺纹设计的钛植入体对骨愈合的影响。
summary_zh.method: 在兔胫骨中植入三种不同螺纹形态的钛植入体，两个月后测量扭矩、骨接触率等。
summary_zh.result: 长螺纹愈合腔设计提高了骨面积分数和骨细胞密度，但扭矩和骨接触率无显著差异。
summary_zh.validation: 通过动物实验和组织学切片验证。

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate the influence of healing chamber configurations in dental implant threads on osseointegration and biomechanical performance.
summary_en.method: Three titanium implant designs (V-thread, square thread, and long healing chamber thread) were implanted in rabbit tibiae, and after two months, torque removal value, bone-to-implant contact, bone area fraction, and osteocyte density were measured.
summary_en.result: The healing chamber design significantly increased bone area fraction and osteocyte density compared to conventional designs, but torque removal and bone-to-implant contact did not differ significantly.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed via in vivo animal study with histometric and biomechanical analyses.
